stem.en: A point on the rim of a spinning wheel moves round a circle at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

text.en: It has no acceleration, because its speed is constant.

feedback.en: The speed is constant, but the direction of the velocity keeps changing. A change in direction is a change in velocity.

text.en: It is accelerating, because the direction of its velocity keeps changing.

feedback.en: Right. In uniform circular motion the velocity changes all the time, so the motion is accelerated.

text.en: It accelerates only when the wheel speeds up or slows down.

feedback.en: A change in speed is one kind of acceleration. A change in direction alone is another.

explanation.en: The velocity has a magnitude and a direction. On a circle, the direction changes at every point, so the velocity changes and the point is accelerating, even at constant speed.

hints.en: Is the direction of motion the same at every point of the circle?
